heading: ## Scope
expected:
Introduce phased co-review orchestration: one session accepts an ordered list of artifacts (`--phases spec,plan`, or either alone) instead of one. `accepted` on a non-final phase auto-finalizes that phase and advances a phase cursor rather than terminating; the author binds each phase's artifact at entry (the plan is generated after the spec passes) via a re-engagement handoff. The fixed reviewer cycle cap is replaced by a turn-holder liveness beacon that survives compaction: declared via PreCompact/SessionStart hooks when the provider supports them, inferred from a 20-minute silence threshold otherwise. Per-phase auto-finalization stamps each accepted artifact with the `co_review:` approval block that Spec A's R4P gate consumes.

Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-1377.md

Reuses the existing base protocol, bounded-wait discipline (#1269), and finalization archive unchanged. Scope decomposition happens at Plan per the spec. Depth-Probe / R4P routing is Spec A (tracked separately). Both specs await a co-review pass before implementation.
replacement:
Implement phased multi-artifact review sessions in the standalone `ai-peer-review` package. One review accepts an ordered list of artifact kinds, including `spec,plan` and either kind alone. A non-final `accepted` decision uses the package's current author-owned finalization contract, advances a durable phase cursor, and permits the author to bind the next artifact through a re-engagement handoff instead of terminating the review. The final phase retains the current terminal acceptance and archive behavior.

Do not implement the historical draft's participant-side liveness beacon in this story. Token-free MCP waiting, resident leases, and automatic transport negotiation already ship in `ai-peer-review@0.2.1`; the remaining external wake coordinator and activation-reconciliation work is owned by the migrated #1517 story in the standalone repository. Phased orchestration must consume those transport boundaries without duplicating them or making provider transcript state authoritative.

The historical design is preserved at AITM commit `ad944209e2b719e9b0ecadbd1d3d710ceacfb498` in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-1377.md`. It was never merged or ratified, so it is design input only. Planning must rebase its phase model, event names, finalization behavior, and compatibility guarantees onto the current standalone protocol and explicitly resolve its open questions before implementation.

Scope decomposition and demonstrable acceptance criteria happen at Refine and Plan. Depth-Probe and AITM Ready-for-Planning routing remain outside this package story.
